I could continue your analogy. Both video games and movies descend from human activities almost completely independent from technology: games (including sports) and theater.

Now, what movies tried to accomplish that theaters couldn't was the reproducibility of moving images (and later sounds) with machines, no longer needing people building stages, wearing costumes and playing music. This result was accomplished almost as soon as the new media was introduced; whatever comes after, is just icing on top of the cake because no matter how much you use CGI or 3D, a movie is still a movie: recorded images and sound.

When video games were introduced, the aim was to reproduce both playful physical activities (such as playing tennis alone against a wall) and old board games (such as chess), apparently doing what movies did compared to theater (automated and reproducible moving images and sounds without people making them), but with a completely different goal: entertain the user with interaction and the classic triad of goals/rules/obstacles that distinguish games from any other pastime.

The big difference here is that video games keep pushing their boundaries farther and farther while movies are basically doing the same thing over and over again, just with better sensory outputs. First we had games requiring more and more timing and dedication, then games that put you in control of a definite character with multiple abilities and nuances, then the simulation of reality started to get quite convincing, then we had interactive stories, and here's where the two media join: video games managed to introduce interaction inside narrative, something movie will never be able to do because it's too late, video games already own that thing.

But it's a slippery slope if you stop caring about the game itself, because as it happens for simulation, immersion, eye-candy and so on, narrative is just complementary to a game, none of the above are enough to be a game in themselves. Too much simulation and you have a simulator; too much immersion and you have virtual reality; too much eye-candy and you have a tech demo; too much narrative, and you have a movie with a complicated tv remote.

So, at the end, it's just a matter of how much story and how good the underlying game is before considering anything else. Also, let's face it: most (all?) stories featured in video games are sub par compared to books and TV series, most probably because good writers go were money and creative freedom are, and no matter how much we think stories are important in modern video games, writers are not that important in a game dev team, and the stories they're told to write have mostly ridiculous and uninspiring premises. Which talented writer would want to write dialogues for the umpteenth high-fantasy saga targeted to teens, really? And that even admitting the narrative leves is going slowly up nowadays.

At least that's what I think after 35+ years of gaming (including 20 years as a pen&paper RPG GM). I'm the opposite of that character in The Matrix: where you people see aliens, Navy Seals and elvish princesses, I see the old triad of goals/rules/obstacles, Game Theory, probability and such.

Hey guys, welcome to sub!

This is a sub to share and discuss new album releases of any kind.

Before posting, there are a couple of rules:

  • No piracy please. That means no torrent links.
  • NO FUCKING PIRACY.

Now that the rules are out of the way, here are some guidelines to make things easier around the sub:

  • The first thing your post must contain is the genre of the release. eg: [METAL].
  • The second thing your post must contain is the artist name and album name. eg: Bring Me The Horizon - That's The Spirit.
  • The third thing your post must contain is the link source. eg: [iTunes]
  • The fourth thing your post must contain is the release date. eg: [2015/09/11]
  • That's it.

Example of a post:

[METAL] Bring Me The Horizon - That's The Spirit [iTunes] [2015/09/11]

SITES TO USE

  • iTunes
  • Spotify
  • Deezer
  • Rdio
  • Apple Music
  • Any stream site that's legit

IF YOU'RE GOING TO USE SPOTIFY OR SOMETHING, POST A COMMENT THAT CONTAINS A LINK TO A SITE WHERE PEOPLE CAN BUY THE ALBUM, OR LINKS TO THE ALBUM ON OTHER STREAMING SERVICES.

You can also use this subverse to discuss upcoming albums, just put a [NEWS] tag infront of the post.

I'm gonna add genre flairs later so the posts will look cleaner. Until then, add the genres manually.
